blocks.text: Lincoln Park: streets and boundaries

items.t: Lincoln Park is an established neighbourhood on Port Coquitlam's north side, and the City's Official Community Plan (OCP) counts Lincoln Park among the city's established neighbourhoods dating from the 1950s.

Coast Meridian Road is the pocket's western spine and Lincoln Avenue its namesake street: Hyde Creek Nature Reserve is at 1457 Lincoln Drive, and the Hyde Creek Recreation Centre and Minnekhada Middle School stand side by side on Laurier Avenue at 1379 and 1390 Laurier Avenue.
Hyde Creek runs through the pocket, which is why so much of Lincoln Park's public land is creek corridor rather than built lots.

blocks.text: Lincoln Park: the housing stock

items.t: The stock is an established post-war detached-house pocket: the City's OCP places Lincoln Park's origins in the 1950s, which makes it one of the older house areas on Port Coquitlam's north side rather than a new subdivision.

The pocket's non-house stock clusters on its edges: the recreation centre, the middle school and the creek reserve occupy the Laurier Avenue and Lincoln Drive frontage, so the interior streets are houses while the services sit on the creek corridor.

blocks.text: Lincoln Park: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Hyde Creek brings a development permit check with it: the City's OCP carries watercourse and hazard development permit areas, and lots touching the Hyde Creek corridor are the ones in this pocket where a permit area can apply before land is altered.

Small-scale multi-unit housing is a city-wide permission with a creek exception to test here: the City permits three to six small-scale units on most RS (Residential Small-Scale) lots without rezoning, with the number set by lot size, location and transit proximity — but a creek-side Lincoln Park lot still has to clear its watercourse conditions first.

blocks.text: Lincoln Park: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Two City institutions share one street: the Hyde Creek Recreation Centre at 1379 Laurier Avenue and Minnekhada Middle School at 1390 Laurier Avenue face each other across the pocket's main service corridor.
Hyde Creek Nature Reserve, at 1457 Lincoln Drive, is listed in the City's parks directory — the creek corridor is protected parkland, not leftover vacant land awaiting development.

Leigh Elementary, the elementary school returned for the Laurier Avenue sample address, is itself across the city boundary at 1230 Soball Street, Coquitlam — a Lincoln Park child's elementary school can sit in the neighbouring city while remaining in the same school district.
Terry Fox Secondary, the secondary school for the pocket, is not in the pocket: it stands at 1260 Riverwood Gate, in the Riverwood area to the southeast.

blocks.text: Lincoln Park: development and new projects

items.t: Hyde Creek Drainage and Culvert Upgrades, Hyde Creek at Coast Meridian Road and Lincoln Avenue, City of Port Coquitlam capital project, drainage and road work: construction of bridges over Coast Meridian Road and Lincoln Avenue, paving, curb and gutter and sidewalk replacement, and storm main, sanitary main and watermain replacement — status: design, construction year 2027 (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Lincoln Park: costs and taxes

items.t: One city-wide figure affects every Lincoln Park bill equally: the City's 2026 property tax increase is 1.95 per cent, and 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026.

blocks.text: Lincoln Park: getting around

items.t: Route 188 is the pocket's spine bus: from Port Coquitlam Station via Coast Meridian Road — stopping at Lincoln Avenue, Patricia Avenue and Laurier Avenue — then David Avenue and Pinetree Way, past Lafarge Lake-Douglas and Lincoln SkyTrain stations, to Coquitlam Central Station.

Route 173 reaches the pocket's southwestern streets: it runs via Westwood Street and Kingsway Avenue to Port Coquitlam Station, then continues via Prairie Avenue and Cedar Drive to Rocklin, interlining with route 174.
Coast Meridian Road is the driving spine: it connects the pocket south to Lougheed Highway and Port Coquitlam Station and north to David Avenue and Coquitlam.

blocks.text: Lincoln Park: risks and due diligence

items.t: Creek proximity is the first check: lots near Hyde Creek can fall in the OCP watercourse development permit area, and the City is designing drainage and culvert upgrades on this creek precisely because it carries stormwater through the pocket.

Drainage work is scheduled, not hypothetical: the Hyde Creek project's bridge, storm main and watermain scope at Coast Meridian Road and Lincoln Avenue carries a 2027 construction year, so buyers on those frontages should expect construction and check the capital projects page for status changes.

Older-house checks apply here: because the OCP dates this neighbourhood to the 1950s, a buyer should expect era-typical servicing and materials questions on interior lots and confirm permit history with the City rather than assuming upgrades were permitted.

blocks.text: Lincoln Park home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

13 houses sold in Lincoln Park with a median price of $1,290,000 (the middle half sold between $1,165,000 and $1,400,000), taking a median of 34 days to sell at 97.9% of the last list price; 8% sold above list. They had a median $576 per square foot, a median year built of 1975 and a median lot of 6,000 square feet. 4 townhomes sold in Lincoln Park, too few (5 needed) to give a typical price.
